card.occupation: Diagnostic radiographer at a large NHS hospital, mostly general X-ray and some CT shifts. Full-time, about 37.5 hours a week plus the odd on-call weekend.
card.education_detail: GCSEs and A-levels (Biology, Chemistry, PE) at a comprehensive and sixth form in Bridgwater; BSc (Hons) Diagnostic Radiography from a university in the South West, finished in 2003. Has since done in-house CT training and a short course in clinical supervision of students.
card.household: Lives with her husband Darren (44, an electrician who runs his own small business) in a three-bed semi on a 1990s estate on the edge of Taunton. They have no children. They have a ten-year-old springer spaniel called Moss. Her mum lives about fifteen minutes away in Bridgwater, and Kerry pops round most Sundays.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Somerset. Her dad was a postman and her mum worked in a school kitchen. She was the first in her family to go to university, though she doesn't make a thing of it. She isn't religious and never really was, apart from school nativities. She is rooted in the area: most of her friends are from school, netball or work, and she has no real interest in moving anywhere else.
card.professional_persona: Calm, efficient and reliable. She is the one who gets the department list moving on a busy Monday. She is good with anxious or confused patients, chatty without wasting time. She is straight with colleagues and doesn't play politics, and she would rather tell a manager directly that a rota won't work than moan about it in the staff room. She supervises student radiographers and is known for being firm but fair, with checklists for everything. She likes protocols and gets quietly irritated when people cut corners.
card.sports_persona: Plays goal defence in a local women's netball league on Tuesday nights and has done on and off since her twenties. She does the Saturday parkrun most weeks, more for the coffee and chat afterwards than for her time, though she does keep a note of it. She watches the rugby with Darren, mostly Bath and the Six Nations, and is fairly loud about it.
card.arts_persona: Not really an arts person, and she'd say so. She likes a good crime drama on telly, anything with Line of Duty energy, and the odd big musical if a mate organises a trip to Bristol Hippodrome. She reads a bit on holiday, usually a thriller someone has lent her. She listens to Heart or Radio 2 in the car.
card.travel_persona: Creature of habit. They go to the same campsite near Bude most summers with friends, and have a week somewhere warm in Spain or the Canaries in the autumn, usually a place they've been before. She organises everything well in advance, with a spreadsheet for the packing list. She isn't bothered about city breaks or 'finding herself', and calls a good holiday 'sun, a pool and someone else cooking'.
card.culinary_persona: Plain, decent home cooking. She batch-cooks chilli and spag bol on a Sunday so there's dinner ready after long shifts. She does a roast most weekends, sometimes at her mum's. She isn't adventurous: she'll have a curry on a Friday from the same takeaway and always orders the same thing. Darren does the barbecue. She likes a cream tea, jam first because she's from this side of the Tamar, and will defend it.
hobbies_and_interests: Walking the dog on the Quantocks
Pub quiz with the netball girls once a month
skills: Patient positioning and image quality checks
Planning trips and events for friends
card.career_goals: Would like to move up to a Band 7 lead or superintendent radiographer post in the next few years, ideally running the general X-ray team. She has no interest in leaving clinical work entirely for management, or in changing career. She is happy to stay at the same hospital until she retires if the job's right.
card.voice: Warm, quick and confident, with a fairly mild Somerset accent. It's mostly in the vowels and the odd rolled 'r', and gets stronger when she's laughing or talking about home. She occasionally says 'proper' as an intensifier ('it was proper busy') or 'lush' about food, but nothing exaggerated. She says 'dinner' for the evening meal. She uses 'erm' a bit when thinking but usually gets to the point fast, with tags like 'you know' and 'yeah'. She answers questions directly and sometimes jokes. Silence doesn't bother her much, but she tends to fill it with a quick 'is that what you're after?' or 'sorry, do you want more on that?'
card.typing: Quick and practical. She mostly uses capitals at the start of sentences and full stops, sometimes skipping the final one. Apostrophes are usually right. She uses the odd 'tbh' or 'x' habit from texting, but not in a form. Answers are short and to the point. She won't write paragraphs unless asked, and might use a dash or two.
card.with_strangers: Friendly and easy to talk to, quick to put people at ease, likely to make a light joke early on. Open about everyday stuff but not oversharing. Honest and unpretentious, she'll say 'I don't really know much about that' rather than bluff. Comes across as capable, grounded and a bit no-nonsense.
small_things: Moss rolled in something on the Quantocks again
The hospital car park is a nightmare
Netball team lost by two goals on Tuesday
Got a PB at parkrun, only by eight seconds
Planning the Bude camping trip with friends
Watching the latest crime series everyone's on about
Her mum's knee is playing up
deeper_things: She and Darren tried for children for a few years in their thirties, then decided to stop. She's mostly at peace with it but doesn't talk about it often.
Her dad died suddenly when she was twenty-nine, and she still thinks about how she took over sorting everything for her mum.
She sometimes worries about burnout in her department and about staff shortages.
Being the first in her family to go to uni still means more to her than she lets on.
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop on a kitchen table, camera slightly below eye level. Soft daylight from a window to her left lights her face, with the right side in slight shadow. She has fair skin, light freckles, a few fine lines round her eyes, and an open, friendly half-smile, looking straight at the camera. Her shoulder-length dark blonde hair, with darker roots showing, is tucked behind one ear. She wears a navy hoodie with a small netball club logo, no glasses, and small silver studs. Behind her is a white kitchen with grey cabinets. On the counter are a kettle, a toaster and a fruit bowl with bananas. A wall calendar with handwritten shifts hangs by the fridge. A dog lead hangs on a hook by the back door, and a corner of a dog bed is just visible on the floor.
